title: The Last Will at Briar House
setting: Briar House, a fictional New England manufacturing town, 1893. A respectable household hides fierce arguments over money. Inspired loosely by the atmosphere surrounding the Borden case, with invented characters, crime and solution.
intro:
Cecily Harcourt has gathered family, staff and advisers at Briar House for an announcement. She is changing her will and dismissing the person who has been managing her accounts.

A charitable trust will receive much of her fortune. Nobody knows how much remains for the family. The new document waits in her study; the old one is displayed in the drawing room.

At eight, Cecily says she will fetch the final account book. "Respectability," she remarks, "is an expensive disguise." The front gate is locked for the evening. Everyone has a reason to worry.

Three readers carry the investigation: Edmund Pell, Ada March and Iris Shaw. The host reads every supplied account, including those from absent neighbors. Discuss only released evidence; nobody invents a private history or a new discovery.

victim.name: Cecily Harcourt
victim.description: Widowed owner of a textile fortune, determined to put her accounts and household in order.

rounds.title: Round 1 - The Bell After the Footsteps
rounds.narration:
Cecily goes into her study before the family announcement. The bell sounds. Ada sees Edmund Pell leave the study before its ringing finishes, carrying a folded legal document. Iris enters afterward and finds Cecily dead. The new will is missing; an account page has been torn out.

Earlier Pell signed Iris's receipt book when collecting the will for the meeting. Beatrice knew her mother had a private appointment before the gathering. Pell says he never entered the study and heard the bell from the drawing room. Set his statement beside the receipt and the corridor sighting; do not settle the timing yet.

Read the first clues. Arguments, threatened jobs and debts make the household uneasy. The missing papers and sequence around the body are more specific than a general family quarrel.

The host reads the original neighbors' recorded responses:
Edmund Pell's recorded response: "I learned Iris Shaw found Cecily after the bell; the receipt records an earlier handover of the missing will. I question her document access, but that signature points to another holder."
Beatrice Harcourt's recorded response: "I heard Ada March was near the study corridor before the alarm, then saw someone leave during ringing. Cecily's account check threatened her job. I wonder why she delayed her account."
Ada March's recorded response: "I heard Felix Harcourt shout before supper that the new will would ruin him; debt notices explain his fear. I want the surviving document, not a shouted rumor."
Iris Shaw's recorded response: "I heard Beatrice Harcourt argue with Cecily about inheritance control this afternoon; a private appointment followed before the alarm. I'm troubled, but when did that meeting happen and those papers disappear?"
Felix Harcourt's recorded response: "I read Edmund Pell's signed will receipt before Cecily's meeting; Ada saw him leave the study with a folded document before the bell stopped. I can't reconcile his denial of entry."

Ada March saw Pell leave before the bell stopped.

Sylvia Grey reported Cecily wanted to repay loyalty, not punish her family.
Dr. Rowan Hale reported Cecily was alert before entering the study.
Nora Bellamy described the proposed trust as support for injured workers.
Julian Finch held an invitation announcing a charitable trust.
Marian Vale reported Cecily planned a private meeting with Pell.

rounds.title: Round 2 - The Copy in the Tray
rounds.narration:
Iris produces the duplicate will from her correspondence tray. The family still inherits. Pell is removed as trustee and must account for unexplained withdrawals. A rumor that Cecily cut off her heirs is now testable against an actual document.

Beatrice brings out the letter she concealed while deciding whether to confront the adviser publicly: "Pell must return what he has taken, or tomorrow I go to the bank." Her argument with Cecily concerned control of her inheritance. Ada admits taking a small household sum to help her brother; it is a different account from the trust.

Read the clues. What could somebody lose through the announcement? A duplicate survives, so stealing the original will cannot change its terms. The scale and recipient of the missing money still need checking.

The host reads the original neighbors' recorded responses:
Edmund Pell's recorded response: "I learned Felix Harcourt borrowed under a false promise without reading the will. I don't trust his disinheritance guess dressed as fact."
Beatrice Harcourt's recorded response: "I learned Iris Shaw planned to leave without telling us. I found her duplicate will in the correspondence tray. Why keep important papers?"
Ada March's recorded response: "I learned Beatrice Harcourt hid Cecily's account letter. After their argument, I wonder whether hiding that warning means money mattered more than reconciliation."
Iris Shaw's recorded response: "I read the duplicate removing Edmund Pell as trustee; Cecily demands repayment before visiting the bank. I see him losing most, not the heirs."
Felix Harcourt's recorded response: "I learned Ada March delayed her corridor account, fearing investigation. Missing household money makes me suspicious of that delay."

rounds.title: Round 4 - A Sound Is Not a Clock
rounds.narration:
Ada demonstrates how the bell mechanism continues sounding after the cord is pulled. Someone already leaving the study can hear it from the corridor. Pell's claim to have heard it elsewhere does not establish where he was when it started.

Iris explains that Cecily ordered her to keep copies, and that she planned to leave her job with a reference. Her retained papers are not evidence that she stole the will. The nephew had never read the document he complained about. Cecily also wrote professional complaints, but those letters remained on the desk while the will and financial page disappeared.

Hear every clue. Return to the receipt, the folded document and the exit before the bell stopped. Each was introduced before this explanation of the mechanism; no new attacker is being squeezed into the timeline.

The host reads the original neighbors' recorded responses:
Edmund Pell's recorded response: "I heard Ada March say the bell sounds after the pull. Her corridor sighting could challenge an alibi, not time a later attack. I worry her account-investigation fears delayed it."
Beatrice Harcourt's recorded response: "I read the appointment naming Edmund Pell and the secretary's receipt for his will collection. He denies the meeting. I can't accept hearing a continuing bell elsewhere as an answer."
Ada March's recorded response: "I see Iris Shaw's duplicate will contradicting the inheritance rumor. Keeping papers while preparing to leave looks like theft to me, until I hear Cecily's instructions about copies."
Iris Shaw's recorded response: "I read that Felix Harcourt still gets enough for his debts. The adviser encouraged his complaints before supper. I wonder whether that false rumor needed a public voice."
Felix Harcourt's recorded response: "I read the duplicate: Beatrice Harcourt still inherits; her hidden letter demands Pell repay money. I see an argument over control, not the adviser's fear of repayment."

rounds.title: Round 5 - The Appointment Kept
rounds.narration:
Beatrice reads the appointment note: Pell was to meet Cecily in the study before the bell and the public announcement. It agrees with the receipt for the new will. Ada reports no other person entering between that meeting and Iris discovering the body.

The daughter was not disinherited. The nephew guessed at the will. Ada's small theft and the physician's surviving complaint explain real disputes, not the removal of trust records. Iris's copies were made on Cecily's orders, before her death. These are corrections to earlier suspicions, not sudden claims that everybody was safely elsewhere.

Read the evidence aloud. The appointment and corridor account undermine Pell's denial of entering the study. The original will is gone, but the missing account page has a surviving carbon copy ready for the final comparison.

The host reads the original neighbors' recorded responses:
Edmund Pell's recorded response: "I read the new will still provides for Beatrice Harcourt. Her saved letter and appointment expose the adviser's repayment trouble. I can't blame that targeted account page on resentment alone."
Beatrice Harcourt's recorded response: "I read the duplicate: Felix Harcourt gets enough for his debts; Pell encouraged his complaints before supper. He's dishonest, but I won't turn that false inheritance rumor into truth."
Ada March's recorded response: "I know Edmund Pell collected the will and left before the bell stopped. Continued ringing doesn't place him elsewhere for me. Repayment letter and appointment still need explaining after that inheritance rumor collapses."
Iris Shaw's recorded response: "I learned Ada March took a small household sum, separate from the trust transfers. I can check her report of no intervening entry against the receipt and appointment."
Felix Harcourt's recorded response: "I learned Cecily ordered Iris Shaw to keep copies. The carbon survives the torn original, naming trust payments to a private practice. I can't explain those transfers by her leaving."

rounds.title: Round 7 - The Money Beneath the Ink
rounds.narration:
The carbon copy is placed under the lamp. It records transfers from Cecily's trust to Edmund Pell's private practice. Beside the total Cecily wrote, "Confront Pell tonight." The sums are not Ada's household shortfall or an inheritance being withheld from a child.

Compare the copy with the repayment letter, appointment, signed receipt and folded document seen leaving the study. The bell mechanism explains why its sound continued after the departure; it cannot erase the meeting. The missing original page could conceal a transfer only if the copy had not survived.

Read every last clue. You have heard the financial motive, access and timing in public. Decide which explanation fits the whole chain rather than relying on a private confession or choosing the loudest family argument.

The host reads the original neighbors' recorded responses:
Edmund Pell's recorded response: "I learned Iris Shaw kept copies on Cecily's orders: transfers and the instruction to confront Pell. I see evidence protected, not hoarded. Leaving doesn't explain payments to someone else's practice."
Beatrice Harcourt's recorded response: "I heard Ada March saw a folded legal document leave the study, with no intervening entry. Her small theft's separate. I can check the delayed sighting against appointment and receipt."
Ada March's recorded response: "I know Felix Harcourt's debts and false promises remain, but the duplicate disproves disinheritance. I wonder if encouraging his complaints drew us away from the trustee's accounts."
Iris Shaw's recorded response: "I see Beatrice Harcourt's saved appointment naming the adviser; her argument seemed suspicious. The will corrects disinheritance, the letter redirects money worries. I don't confuse independence with keeping stolen trust funds."
Felix Harcourt's recorded response: "I read the carbon: trust money reached Edmund Pell's private practice; Cecily demanded repayment and arranged his denied meeting. Receipt, appointment and exit sighting contradict Edmund Pell. I see torn originals, not erased copies."

finale.narration: The front gate opens as the constable arrives. Before anyone hands over a name, explain the money trail and the false timeline. A family quarrel is not enough. Which person needed the new will and its accounts to disappear?
finale.votePrompt: Who murdered Cecily Harcourt at Briar House?

solution.explanation: Pell killed Cecily during the study meeting to conceal trust transfers to his private practice. The carbon copy names the recipient, and the earlier repayment letter and duplicate will explain the impending loss of his trusteeship. His signed receipt, the appointment note and Ada's exit account contradict his denial of entering. The continuing bell explains why it was still sounding after he left; it does not supply an alibi. The folded document and selectively missing will and account page fit the attempted concealment, while copies made beforehand survived. Family quarrels and smaller thefts cannot explain the complete money, document and timing chain. This is a fictional solution, not a claim about the real Borden case.
solution.revealNarration: The room returns to the records and observations it heard aloud. The murderer is Edmund Pell. No confession is needed: the public evidence tells the story.

hiddenThread: A continuing bell and selectively missing legal papers conceal a chain of trust transfers behind the inheritance rumors.
coverageRepeatNote: The trio covers its six directed pairs in the first two rounds. Later repeats add released evidence or explicitly correct earlier assumptions. Supporting readers cover all other selected targets before repeating, never consecutively. The separate singleton readings preserve the trio without changing the master.
specialMechanics: Bell-timing test: the bell can establish that a mechanism sounded, not who was present; compare it with independent corridor records.

readAloud.observation: I read the appointment naming {solicitor} and the secretary's receipt for his will collection.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: He denies the meeting. I can't accept hearing a continuing bell elsewhere as an answer.

readAloud.text: I read the duplicate: {nephew} gets enough for his debts; Pell encouraged his complaints before supper. He's dishonest, but I won't turn that false inheritance rumor into truth.
readAloud.observation: I read the duplicate: {nephew} gets enough for his debts; Pell encouraged his complaints before supper.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: He's dishonest, but I won't turn that false inheritance rumor into truth.

readAloud.text: I heard {housekeeper} saw a folded legal document leave the study, with no intervening entry. Her small theft's separate. I can check the delayed sighting against appointment and receipt.
readAloud.observation: I heard {housekeeper} saw a folded legal document leave the study, with no intervening entry.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Her small theft's separate. I can check the delayed sighting against appointment and receipt.

readAloud.text: I heard {nephew} shout before supper that the new will would ruin him; debt notices explain his fear. I want the surviving document, not a shouted rumor.
readAloud.observation: I heard {nephew} shout before supper that the new will would ruin him; debt notices explain his fear.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I want the surviving document, not a shouted rumor.

readAloud.text: I learned {daughter} hid Cecily's account letter. After their argument, I wonder whether hiding that warning means money mattered more than reconciliation.
readAloud.observation: I learned {daughter} hid Cecily's account letter.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: After their argument, I wonder whether hiding that warning means money mattered more than reconciliation.

readAloud.text: I see {secretary}'s duplicate will contradicting the inheritance rumor. Keeping papers while preparing to leave looks like theft to me, until I hear Cecily's instructions about copies.
readAloud.observation: I see {secretary}'s duplicate will contradicting the inheritance rumor.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Keeping papers while preparing to leave looks like theft to me, until I hear Cecily's instructions about copies.

readAloud.text: I know {solicitor} collected the will and left before the bell stopped. Continued ringing doesn't place him elsewhere for me. Repayment letter and appointment still need explaining after that inheritance rumor collapses.
readAloud.observation: I know {solicitor} collected the will and left before the bell stopped.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Continued ringing doesn't place him elsewhere for me. Repayment letter and appointment still need explaining after that inheritance rumor collapses.

readAloud.text: I know {nephew}'s debts and false promises remain, but the duplicate disproves disinheritance. I wonder if encouraging his complaints drew us away from the trustee's accounts.
readAloud.observation: I know {nephew}'s debts and false promises remain, but the duplicate disproves disinheritance.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I wonder if encouraging his complaints drew us away from the trustee's accounts.

readAloud.text: I heard {daughter} argue with Cecily about inheritance control this afternoon; a private appointment followed before the alarm. I'm troubled, but when did that meeting happen and those papers disappear?
readAloud.observation: I heard {daughter} argue with Cecily about inheritance control this afternoon; a private appointment followed before the alarm.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I'm troubled, but when did that meeting happen and those papers disappear?

readAloud.text: I read the duplicate removing {solicitor} as trustee; Cecily demands repayment before visiting the bank. I see him losing most, not the heirs.
readAloud.observation: I read the duplicate removing {solicitor} as trustee; Cecily demands repayment before visiting the bank.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I see him losing most, not the heirs.

readAloud.text: I read that {nephew} still gets enough for his debts. The adviser encouraged his complaints before supper. I wonder whether that false rumor needed a public voice.
readAloud.observation: I read that {nephew} still gets enough for his debts.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The adviser encouraged his complaints before supper. I wonder whether that false rumor needed a public voice.

readAloud.text: I learned {housekeeper} took a small household sum, separate from the trust transfers. I can check her report of no intervening entry against the receipt and appointment.
readAloud.observation: I learned {housekeeper} took a small household sum, separate from the trust transfers.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I can check her report of no intervening entry against the receipt and appointment.

readAloud.text: I see {daughter}'s saved appointment naming the adviser; her argument seemed suspicious. The will corrects disinheritance, the letter redirects money worries. I don't confuse independence with keeping stolen trust funds.
readAloud.observation: I see {daughter}'s saved appointment naming the adviser; her argument seemed suspicious.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The will corrects disinheritance, the letter redirects money worries. I don't confuse independence with keeping stolen trust funds.

readAloud.text: I read {solicitor}'s signed will receipt before Cecily's meeting; Ada saw him leave the study with a folded document before the bell stopped. I can't reconcile his denial of entry.
readAloud.observation: I read {solicitor}'s signed will receipt before Cecily's meeting; Ada saw him leave the study with a folded document before the bell stopped.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I can't reconcile his denial of entry.

readAloud.text: I learned {housekeeper} delayed her corridor account, fearing investigation. Missing household money makes me suspicious of that delay.
readAloud.observation: I learned {housekeeper} delayed her corridor account, fearing investigation.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Missing household money makes me suspicious of that delay.

readAloud.text: I read the duplicate: {daughter} still inherits; her hidden letter demands Pell repay money. I see an argument over control, not the adviser's fear of repayment.
readAloud.observation: I read the duplicate: {daughter} still inherits; her hidden letter demands Pell repay money.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I see an argument over control, not the adviser's fear of repayment.

readAloud.text: I learned Cecily ordered {secretary} to keep copies. The carbon survives the torn original, naming trust payments to a private practice. I can't explain those transfers by her leaving.
readAloud.observation: I learned Cecily ordered {secretary} to keep copies.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The carbon survives the torn original, naming trust payments to a private practice. I can't explain those transfers by her leaving.

readAloud.text: I read the carbon: trust money reached {solicitor}'s private practice; Cecily demanded repayment and arranged his denied meeting. Receipt, appointment and exit sighting contradict {solicitor}. I see torn originals, not erased copies.
readAloud.observation: I read the carbon: trust money reached {solicitor}'s private practice; Cecily demanded repayment and arranged his denied meeting.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Receipt, appointment and exit sighting contradict {solicitor}. I see torn originals, not erased copies.
